lessons.title: Identifying relative clauses with who, which and that
lessons.explanation: A relative clause says which person or thing you mean. Use who for people, which for things and that for either: The woman who lives next door is a nurse. This is the book which I bought. The man that called is my uncle. The relative word replaces the noun, so do not add another pronoun: not The book which I bought it.

examples.en: The woman who lives next door is a nurse.
This is the book which I bought.
The man that called is my uncle.

lessons.title: Connectors for cause, time and result
lessons.explanation: Connectors link short clauses. Use because for a reason: I stayed home because I was ill. Use so for a result: I was ill, so I stayed home. Use when, before and after for time: Call me when you arrive. Wash your hands before you eat. Because answers why; so gives the result. Do not use both because and so in one sentence.

examples.en: I stayed home because I was ill.
I was ill, so I stayed home.
Call me when you arrive.

lessons.title: First conditional for likely possibilities
lessons.explanation: Use if plus the present simple for a likely condition and will plus the base verb for its result: If it rains, we will stay at home. The if-clause uses the present, not will: not If it will rain. You can put the if-clause second without a comma: We will stay at home if it rains. Questions: What will you do if you miss the bus?

lessons.title: Reporting statements and requests
lessons.explanation: To report what someone says now, use says that plus a clause: She says that she is tired. The word that is optional. Change the pronoun when the speaker changes: 'I am tired' becomes She says she is tired. To report a request or order use asked or told plus an object plus to and the base verb: He asked me to open the door. She told us not to be late.

examples.en: She says that she is tired.
He asked me to open the door.
She told us not to be late.

pt.title: Relatando afirmações e pedidos
pt.explanation: Para relatar o que alguém diz no presente, use says that mais uma oração: She says that she is tired. That é opcional. Mude o pronome quando a pessoa que fala mudar: 'I am tired' vira She says she is tired. Para relatar um pedido ou uma ordem, use asked ou told mais um objeto, seguido de to e da forma base do verbo: He asked me to open the door. She told us not to be late.

examples.en: She says that she is tired.
examples.pt: Ela diz que está cansada.

examples.en: He asked me to open the door.
examples.pt: Ele me pediu para abrir a porta.

examples.en: She told us not to be late.
examples.pt: Ela nos disse para não nos atrasarmos.

lessons.title: Reporting statements and requests
lessons.explanation: To report what someone says now, use says that plus a clause: She says that she is tired. The word that is optional. Change the pronoun when the speaker changes: 'I am tired' becomes She says she is tired. To report a request or order use asked or told plus an object plus to and the base verb: He asked me to open the door. She told us not to be late.

examples.en: She says that she is tired.
He asked me to open the door.
She told us not to be late.
